question: Is AM's Phase-2 write storing document CONTENT at all, or is a large part of the measured MT 'acquisition' a content-free distribution/format shift caused by perturbing the cartridge at all?
variable_under_test: SYNTH_DATA_PATH = which documents get written (arm A canonical MT corpus [reused] vs arm B the Phase-1 QA-topic corpus, which contains NO MT content by construction vs arm C the same 16 MT documents in REVERSED write order). Everything else canonical: TOP_T=32, GRANULARITY=per_layer, SLOT_SELECTION=tfidf, USE_IDF=0, KEY_MODE=freeze, TARGET_MODE=cartridge_plus_doc, RIDGE_LAMBDA=1e-4, RIDGE_SCALE=spectral, DELTA_WEIGHT=1e-2, MAX_QUERIES_PER_HEAD=64, MAX_REF_EXAMPLES_PER_DOC=32, AM_EXECUTION_MODE=per_document, Phase-1 cache outputs/phase1_selfdistill_qwen512/cache_last.pt. No source file edited.
baseline_ref: arm A = EXP-007-top32 / DIAG-OVERWRITE canonical run (run dir 2026-07-28-21-43-17-continual_am_sparse/4b0edcab-...), per-k curve from DIAG-SEQUENCE; Phase-1 floor QA 2.23880672454834 / MT 3.7825491428375244 re-measured in-session and reproduced to all 16 digits

diagnostics.verdict: The acquisition claim SURVIVES, but only partially and with a large content-free component. Writing 16 documents that contain NO MT content lowers MT loss by 0.348 at the canonical operating point k=16 (28.3% of the canonical 1.230 improvement) and by 0.785 at its own optimum k=8 (63.8% of the canonical total, 73.2% of what canonical achieves at the SAME k). All of these are far outside the +-0.15 noise band. At the same time, real MT content is worth a real and measurable amount: at every matched k>=4 the canonical arm beats the content-free arm by 0.232 / 0.288 / 0.608 / 0.882 loss (k=4/8/12/16), every one outside the noise band.

content_free_fraction_of_the_1.23_mt_imp.read: between 28% (strict endpoint, k=16) and 64% (arm B's own optimum) of the canonical MT improvement is reproducible with documents that share zero content with the MT eval

order_control_arm_C.verified_by_slug: arm C's per-document slugs are exactly arm A's reversed (arm A doc-000=ae4e8fb7 / doc-015=af07b880; arm C doc-000=af07b880 / doc-015=ae4e8fb7)
order_control_arm_C.read: holding content EXACTLY constant and changing only the sequence moves MT by +0.340 at k=16 -- outside the noise band and comparable in size to the entire content-free gain of arm B. Write order is a first-class determinant of the reported MT number.

diagnostics.arm_B_curve_shape: non-monotone: MT is slightly WORSE than Phase-1 after one document (3.7952 vs 3.7825, inside noise), falls to a minimum 2.9978 at k=8, then RISES to 3.0436 at k=12 and 3.4343 at k=16. The content-free gain accumulates over the first ~8 writes and is then eaten by cumulative damage. Canonical falls monotonically to k=12 and rises only over the last four.
diagnostics.arm_B_qa_axis: arm B writes the exact 16 papers the QA eval scores (16/16 title overlap), so its QA number is NOT a retention measure -- it is re-writing the very content being scored. It still DEGRADES QA at every k (+0.097 / +0.022 / +0.097 / +0.265 / +0.652 above the Phase-1 floor at k=1/4/8/12/16). Writing a paper into the cartridge makes the model WORSE at that paper.

no_op_confound_REFUTED_BY_MEASUREMENT.concern: the Phase-1 cartridge was BUILT from the QA corpus, so writing it back might be closer to a no-op than a perturbation, which would UNDERSTATE the content-free effect
no_op_confound_REFUTED_BY_MEASUREMENT.read: arm B is the LARGEST perturbation of the three -- it displaces 69.9% of the Phase-1 value tensor's Frobenius norm (vs canonical 62.1%) and changes MORE slots (2195 vs 1960). The 'writing it back is a no-op' objection is refuted by direct measurement; if anything arm B is a harsher write than canonical.

mass_on_S.read: all three arms sit within 0.079-0.091 eval-time mass_on_S on MT -- a 13% spread -- while their MT losses differ by 0.882. mass_on_S does not order the arms; arm B has the HIGHEST bandwidth and the WORST MT.

total_cartridge_attention_mass.read: the B-CASCADE routing collapse (0.588 -> 0.329) is SPECIFIC to the canonical arm. Arms B and C leave cartridge mass at or above the Phase-1 level, and the canonical arm -- the one with the collapsed routing and the largest |v| -- has the BEST MT. Routing health and MT are anti-ordered across these three arms.

mt_eval_coverage_by_k.read: arm B covers 0% of the MT eval at every k by construction; arm C's coverage curve is close to canonical's, so the two are comparable at equal k

observations: The QA corpus yields exactly 16 unique documents, so arm B wrote 16 documents -- the same count as canonical -- and its per-document snapshots give a curve directly comparable to DIAG-SEQUENCE's at equal k. THE CLAIM SURVIVES, BUT DAMAGED: writing 16 documents with zero MT content still lowers MT loss from the 3.7825 Phase-1 floor to 3.4343 at k=16 (0.348, 28.3% of the canonical 1.230 improvement) and to 2.9978 at its own optimum k=8 (0.785, 63.8% of the canonical total and 73.2% of what the canonical arm achieves at the same k) -- every one of these far outside the +-0.15 noise band. So a large, measurable fraction of what the loop reports as 'acquisition' is reproducible with documents the eval never asks about. At the same time the content axis is real: at every matched k>=4 the canonical arm beats the content-free arm by 0.232 / 0.288 / 0.608 / 0.882 loss (k=4/8/12/16), all outside the band, and the gap widens with k -- so the write is not purely a format effect. The honest split is: 28% content-free at the reported k=16 operating point, up to 64% at the content-free arm's own optimum. THE OBVIOUS CONFOUND IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT ASSUMED AWAY: writing the QA corpus back into a cartridge that was built from it is NOT a no-op -- arm B displaces 69.9% of the Phase-1 value tensor's Frobenius norm versus canonical's 62.1%, changes MORE slots (2195 vs 1960), and is the harshest of the three writes. It also degrades QA at every k, ending +0.652 above the Phase-1 floor at k=16, even though it is re-writing the exact 16 papers the QA eval scores (16/16 title overlap, verified) -- writing a paper into the cartridge makes the model worse at that paper. THE ORDER CONTROL (arm C) RAN AND IS INFORMATIVE: the same 16 MT documents in reversed order (verified by slug -- arm C's doc-000 is arm A's doc-015) reach MT 2.8920 at k=16 versus canonical 2.5524, a +0.340 penalty from sequence alone with content held exactly constant, outside the noise band and comparable in magnitude to arm B's entire content-free gain; arm C retains 72.4% of the canonical improvement and peaks at k=12 (2.7166) as canonical does. Two internals findings cut against the board's current framing: (i) all three arms sit within 0.079-0.091 eval-time mass_on_S on MT -- a 13% spread -- while their MT losses span 0.882, and the arm with the HIGHEST bandwidth (arm B, 0.0906) has the WORST MT; (ii) the B-CASCADE routing collapse is specific to the canonical arm -- total cartridge attention mass is 0.329 (arm A) versus 0.655 (arm B) and 0.591 (arm C) against a Phase-1 0.588, so across these three arms healthy routing and low MT are anti-ordered. Solve-side: mean_mse 0.11906 / 0.15708 / 0.11961 and |v|max 984 / 760 / 724 for arms A / B / C; solve wall clock 169.3 / 223.0 / 196.0 s; phase2 end-to-end 502 / 426 / 569 s; gradient_steps 0 everywhere. Harness controls all passed in-session: the Phase-1 anchors re-measured to all 16 printed digits (QA 2.23880672454834 / MT 3.7825491428375244), arm A's route-mass reproduced ORACLE-WRITE's control identically (mass_on_S 0.07734 QA / 0.08098 MT, cartridge mass 0.32002 / 0.32853), all 22 evals are confirmed from their logs to have loaded the intended checkpoint, and the frozen snapshot's manifest was byte-identical before and after even though repo HEAD moved mid-run. CAVEATS: arm A's per-k curve is REUSED from DIAG-SEQUENCE and was not re-measured this session (only its Phase-1 anchors and its final-cache routing were); every arm is a single seed and no seed variation was run, so the k at which each curve turns is not seed-varied; k=1 deltas for all three arms sit inside the noise band, so nothing can be concluded about a single write; arm B shares FORMAT (QASPER papers, same synthesis conversation template) with the MT corpus while sharing no content, which is precisely the format-shift hypothesis under test but also means arm B does not bound the effect of writing genuinely out-of-distribution text.
strongest_surviving_objection: Arm B's documents are QASPER papers in the same synthesis format as the MT corpus, differing only in topic. So the 28-64% 'content-free' fraction is really 'topic-free within the same corpus format' -- it does not separate a generic activation-perturbation effect from transfer of shared scientific-paper structure. A truly out-of-distribution write corpus would tighten the bound. Second: arm A's per-k curve was reused rather than re-measured, so the matched-k ratios mix this session's arm B/C evals with DIAG-SEQUENCE's arm A evals (same script, same convention, and the shared Phase-1 anchors matched to 16 digits, but it is not a within-session A/B).
